summary: The solver-visible Stonevault core is a credible crash-safe storage engine: a Rust line-protocol front end over a multi-module C++ WAL/MVCC/snapshot backend with recovery, checkpointing, and cross-layer integrity auditing. Major modules are reachable from the documented operator entrypoint, materially differentiated, and coupled through shared commit-sequence and durability invariants. Roughly 3,300+ lines of runtime/configuration code exceed the large_system_strict substantive LOC floor; toy and high-padding risks are not present, though build-script repetition is mildly inflating config volume.

evidence.observation: Frontier Software/Databases task declaring artifact /app/stonevault, 10800s agent timeout, and workdir /app/stonevault—consistent with a substantial storage-engine work package subject to large_system_strict production-depth floors.

Documents operator entrypoint /app/stonevault/bin/stonevault, READY handshake, transactional command surface, WAL/snapshot on-disk contracts, and HEALTH invariants—establishing real production workflows rather than a single-function stub.
Stdin/stdout REPL loads RuntimeConfig, opens Engine via FFI, emits READY, and dispatches parsed commands through session guards into protocol::execute for every supported operator command.

Engine construction calls restore_database, wires WAL append/sync on commit, catalog MVCC apply_commit, snapshot publish on checkpoint, and exposes full sv_* C API used by Rust FFI for all storage operations.

Implements framed append-only WAL records with CRC validation, torn-tail truncation, pending-transaction replay, and contiguous commit-sequence enforcement during recovery—non-trivial branching persistence logic.
VersionCatalog maintains per-key version histories with tombstones, snapshot-image export, conflict detection helper, prefix scan, and extensive integrity audit accounting over committed sequence.
restore_database orchestrates snapshot load, WAL recover/replay, and next-transaction-id advancement—central cross-module startup path coupling snapshot, WAL, and catalog state.

audit_runtime_state and validate_* routines cross-check catalog snapshots, active transactions, and durable path presence/aliasing; engine stats/health invoke this layer, keeping integrity logic reachable from operator STATS/HEALTH commands.

Build script compiles eleven separate C++ storage translation units into libstonevault_engine.a and links them into the Rust binary—config volume that repeats near-identical g++ invocations per module.

Q6 large_system_strict PASS requires >=3,000 substantive reachable solver-visible runtime/config LOC and no HIGH toy_logic_risk or padding_risk; judgment must be rebuilt from code and interactions, not LOC alone.

findings.criterion: Separate production complexity from generated/vendor/comment/config-volume noise (.terminus/agents/QUALITY_AGENT_PROMPTS.md Q6 method step 8)
findings.why_it_matters: Eleven near-duplicate g++ compile blocks inflate configuration LOC without adding domain behavior, creating mild padding signal even though overall runtime depth remains credible.
findings.minimal_remediation: Refactor build.rs to iterate storage/*.cpp sources in a loop or Makefile rule set while preserving the same linked artifact.
findings.regression_risk: Low if link order and compile flags remain identical.

do_not_change: Rust/C++ boundary split and documented /app/stonevault/bin/stonevault entrypoint
WAL/MVCC/snapshot module decomposition and cross-module recovery/checkpoint coupling
Integrity audit layer invoked from STATS/HEALTH

Intentionally incomplete wiring that defines the repair work (e.g., snapshot CRC verification, writer lock acquisition, transaction overlay on scan, commit conflict checks) unless a separate defect-remediation pass is authorized
next_gate: QUALITY_INTERLOCK aggregate with Q4 Spec-Test Contract Reviewer; Q6 PASS with HIGH confidence and SUFFICIENT evidence satisfies the Q6 predicate when paired with a current Q4 PASS.

role_output.SUBSTANTIVE_LOC_ASSESSMENT: Approximately 1,869 lines of C++ implementation, ~490 lines of storage headers with domain types/constants, and ~990 lines of Rust runtime (protocol, FFI, session, I/O, observability) yield ~3,350 substantive reachable runtime lines; build.rs adds ~110 configuration lines (~90 of which are repetitive compile boilerplate). Excluding that boilerplate still clears the >=3,000 large_system_strict floor.
MAJOR_MODULES: engine: lifecycle orchestration, mutex-guarded mutations, C ABI surface
wal: framed append, fsync commit, recovery with torn-tail repair
catalog: MVCC version histories, scans, snapshot export, conflict helper
snapshot: load/publish snapshot.dat via temp file + rename + directory sync
transactions: active transaction table, write-set overlay helper
integrity: catalog/transaction/storage path audits for STATS/HEALTH
codec: endian serialization, CRC32, hex transcoding, durable I/O helpers
lock/maintenance: writer lock file and data-dir preparation
Rust protocol/session/ffi: ASCII command grammar, session tx tracking, FFI error bridging
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Repairing WAL torn-tail handling without matching snapshot CRC acceptance breaks checkpoint/recovery agreement
Fixing GET local overlay without also wiring SCAN through apply_transaction_overlay leaves inconsistent transactional visibility
Enabling commit conflict detection in catalog.conflicts without WAL ordering/sync semantics can publish or reject commits inconsistently
Tightening HEALTH integrity checks without aligning stats() WAL byte cross-check causes divergent observability surfaces
Implementing writer lock acquisition independently of open/recovery path risks conflicting multi-process durability assumptions
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Deleting wal.cpp+catalog.cpp+recovery.cpp (~650 lines, ~19% of runtime) removes durability, MVCC, and startup replay—core behavior collapses. Deleting integrity.cpp and related audit helpers (~330 lines, ~10%) removes HEALTH/STATS cross-validation while leaving naive mutations. Removing repetitive build.rs blocks (~90 lines) would not change runtime semantics.
role_output.REQUIRED_CHANGES: None for Q6 PASS; optional advisory reduction of build.rs repetition to lower MEDIUM padding_risk.
